verdict.rationale: Mastra documents its own automatic triggers: a workflow `schedule` field fires on a cron, agents can run on a cron cadence, and workflows can pause to wait for an API callback and then resume or bail based on the input. These are time-based triggers and in-run conditional logic, not a general rule engine that starts actions when arbitrary events occur. missing for 10: declarative event-to-action rules, documented event-source triggers (e.g. starting a workflow on incoming events or webhooks), a rule-definition interface for AI-native users, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Declare a `schedule` field on a workflow and Mastra will fire it on the cron you specify.
A schedule runs an agent on a cron cadence.
Pause a workflow at any step to collect additional data, wait for an API callback
The workflow can then either resume or bail based on the input received.
